races.name: Star Sports Handicap

runners_data.name: Killavia
runners_data.note: Front runner returning from 229-day break but has excellent course and distance form with three consecutive improving efforts here last summer
runners_data.spotlight: Improved in three consecutive C&D appearances last summer, finishing third of seven in Listed event before a commanding maiden win (also good; made all) in July; was cast in her box the night before an August assignment after which her trainer recently reported she was never really right; that stable tour also offered hope she's back in a good place and can go well on this handicap debut/reappearance.

runners_data.name: Major Neigh Sayer
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with Oisin Murphy aboard for in-form George Scott yard, though attempting 5f for first time after weakening over longer recently
runners_data.spotlight: Won a 7f Newmarket maiden (good) in October but finished down the field having led in French heavy-ground Listed race next time; weakened when attempting 1m on his comeback in April but this first start at 5f since his 2yo debut is still something of a surprise; fascinating to see what he makes of it in an additional tongue-tie with Oisin Murphy steering.

runners_data.name: Gouken
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits after breakthrough Newcastle win, Ed Walker runner comes here in good form with just 11 days since last encouraging effort
runners_data.spotlight: In the placings on all five starts on a variety of surfaces as a juvenile (6f/7f) and he deservedly made the breakthrough on his reappearance at Newcastle (6f, AW) last month; respectable fifth of 14 at Hamilton on his recent handicap debut and this experiment at 5f looks worth a go.

runners_data.name: Akirra
runners_data.note: Natural front runner who bolted up in Wolverhampton maiden but faces step up in class after 178-day absence under Rossa Ryan
runners_data.spotlight: All starts at 5f; fast turf no problem when runner-up at Windsor (latterly promoted to first) in August and he bolted up in Wolverhampton maiden in November having previously gone quite close on handicap debut at Southwell (also AW); underwhelmed on final start of last term but subsequently gelded and he's in the right hands to progress this season.

runners_data.name: Our Cody
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse carrying top weight returning from 230-day break, but showed good level when Listed-placed and has strong 5f record
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark on her third start when taking a Windsor maiden (good to firm) in June and it was a fine effort when second of 12 in Listed event at Ayr (also 5f, soft) in September; makes her handicap debut on this reappearance and she warrants respect.

runners_data.name: The Lost Sock
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for in-form Roger Varian stable with solid course and distance form, though last run was disappointing at this venue
runners_data.spotlight: Catterick maiden (good) winner in August who was every bit as good when third at Wolverhampton (also 5f, AW; Kolkata Knight second) in March; didn't look to be making much of an impression when the door slammed in his face at Thirsk last time but it's too soon to write him off.

runners_data.name: Kolkata Knight
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who improved after wind surgery but trainer Tom Dascombe having quiet spell with only 1 winner from 11 recent runners
runners_data.spotlight: Landed Hamilton maiden (6f, good to firm) on debut but better form after wind surgery when bagging Haydock handicap (5f, good to soft) in September; subsequently gelded and ran well for second (5f, AW; winner on the middle leg of a hat-trick) on his reappearance, while latest start from a wide stall at Chester can be written off; needs considering.

runners_data.name: Havana Smile
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse best at 5f including good second here in August, but trainers Gary & Josh Moore without a winner from 22 recent attempts
runners_data.spotlight: Sole start at 5f came at this track and it was his best effort too, when second of nine in a maiden (good) in August; last two runs were at 7f and didn't scream he's desperate for this return to 5f; not handicapped out of things, though.

races.paceDynamic: Killavia and Akirra are both confirmed front runners who will contest the early pace from the gates, with Major Neigh Sayer, Gouken, The Lost Sock and Kolkata Knight likely to track just behind in a prominent position. Over this sharp 5f at Sandown, the dual pace angle should create an honest gallop without being overly fierce given the small field size. The race will be run at a solid tempo throughout with the leaders staying involved, but the genuine pace should set it up perfectly for the prominent racers to strike in the final furlong. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can sit just off the pace and pounce late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Strike Gold
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest but sustainable allowing trackers to stay close
scenarios.body: The dual front runners will soften each other up just enough for the prominent racers to come through with perfectly timed challenges. Major Neigh Sayer, Gouken, The Lost Sock and Kolkata Knight are all ideally positioned to benefit from this tactical scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survival
scenarios.trigger: If one of the leaders gets an uncontested lead while the other fades early
scenarios.body: Killavia or Akirra will dominate from the front without serious pace pressure, allowing them to control the tempo and kick clear when it matters. The lack of sustained pressure from a pace rival gives the survivor every chance to hold on.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong and burns out the leaders and prominent trackers
scenarios.body: Our Cody and Havana Smile, both natural hold-up horses, will benefit from a collapse up front as the pace takes its toll. Their patient tactics will pay dividends as they sweep past tiring rivals in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If both front runners go too hard and die dramatically while prominent horses also suffer
scenarios.body: The entire pace dynamic falls apart with leaders and trackers all struggling, creating a messy finish where any horse with energy left can capitalize. This randomizes the outcome and opens the door for any runner with late momentum.

watchPoints.text: Killavia and Akirra must be monitored for how hard they go in the opening two furlongs as excessive pace will set up the race for closers
Major Neigh Sayer dropping back to 5f for the first time could be a negative if Oisin Murphy gets trapped in a pocket behind the leaders
Our Cody carrying top weight of 137lbs after a 230-day absence may find the combination too much to overcome despite her class
The Lost Sock disappointed badly last time at this course and needs to bounce back to her earlier promise for Varian
Trainer form is concerning for Kolkata Knight with Tom Dascombe managing just one winner from eleven recent runners

races.name: Star Sports National Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Dandyman Dan
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly suited to the likely strong pace, though 31 days off and inexperience are mild concerns
runners_data.spotlight: Belied 40-1 odds and evident inexperience to win on last month's debut at Bath (5.7f, firm); likely to improve but others have more substance to their form.

runners_data.name: A Bear Affair
runners_data.note: Another hold-up runner who should benefit from the pace scenario, with Hannon's 27-day gap since Ascot run ideal
runners_data.spotlight: Won the Brocklesby at Doncaster (5f, good to soft) in March and beaten only 1l when third of three to Adaay Of Scarlett at Ascot four weeks ago (5f, good to firm; same terms today); something to find with the winner but might not be far away.

runners_data.name: Napa
runners_data.note: Highest-rated but showed front-running tendencies at Newmarket which could be problematic in this pace battle
runners_data.spotlight: Built upon the promise on last month's debut fourth at Newbury (5f, good) to win valuable novice at Newmarket (5f, good to firm); did it nicely from the front last time and he's a leading contender today.

runners_data.name: Where Love Lives
runners_data.note: Led throughout at Thirsk but faces much stronger pace pressure here with 48 days since last run a slight worry
runners_data.spotlight: Sent off favourite when readily making all at Thirsk (5f, good) last month and that form has been franked by the clear runner-up; this likeable prospect is firmly in calculations.

runners_data.name: Adaay Of Scarlett
runners_data.note: Consistent leader but Murphy's tactical nous may see him drop in just behind the early pace
runners_data.spotlight: Impressive on debut at Newmarket (5f, good) last month and narrowly followed up in a warm, three-runner conditions race at Ascot (5f, good to firm); he could have improvement in him and is one to consider.

runners_data.name: Bill The Bull
runners_data.note: Likely to be outpaced by this quality field despite showing promise in lesser company
runners_data.spotlight: Fourth of 15 to A Bear Affair in the Brocklesby at Doncaster (5f, good to soft) and again showed promise when third at Wolverhampton (5f, AW) recently; having hung right last time he could appreciate having a rail on his right-hand side today, but others have stronger claims.

runners_data.name: Princesse d'Orange
runners_data.note: Did too much too soon in Listed company last time and faces similar pace pressure today
runners_data.spotlight: Easily made all when favourite on debut at Beverley (5f, good to soft) last month; did too much too soon when attempting to repeat those tactics in Listed race at York (5f, good) a fortnight ago, finishing fifth of ten, but she's not written off in view of her initial promise.

runners_data.name: Mr Macartney
runners_data.note: Prominent style could work if he can avoid the early speed battle, though trainer's 0/5 record is concerning
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Leicester (5f, good to firm) last month on second start; faded when seventh of 13 in Newmarket novice (6f, good) and returns to 5f today, but it seems likely that his limitations will again be exposed.

races.paceDynamic: Princesse d'Orange, Where Love Lives, Adaay Of Scarlett, and Bill The Bull will ensure a furious gallop from the start with all four capable of leading. Napa also showed front-running tendencies at Newmarket and could join the pace battle, creating an unsustainable tempo over this minimum trip. The strong pace will stretch the field and test stamina reserves, with the early leaders likely to pay for their exertions. This race shape strongly favours the hold-up horses who can sit off the pace and deliver late challenges when the pace-setters weaken.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the four confirmed front-runners engage in a pace duel from the start
scenarios.body: The furious early gallop will set up the race perfectly for Dandyman Dan and A Bear Affair to close from the rear. Both have shown they can quicken when produced late and will benefit from others doing the donkey work.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Napa controls from prominent
scenarios.trigger: If Napa can sit just off the leaders rather than making the running
scenarios.body: David Egan can use his horse's class advantage to track the pace-setters before delivering a sustained challenge. The OR 101 rating gives him a significant edge if he can avoid the early burn-up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Adaay dominates throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Adaay Of Scarlett can establish an early advantage and dictate terms
scenarios.body: His two impressive wins show he has the class to sustain pressure, and Oisin Murphy's tactical awareness could see him steal a march. The consistent good going form gives him every chance to repeat his Ascot success.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses completely
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is even more suicidal than expected and all leaders stop
scenarios.body: Mr Macartney's prominent style could prove ideal as he sits closer than the pure hold-up horses but avoids the early speed duel. His recent Leicester win shows he has the ability when conditions suit.

watchPoints.text: Watch Princesse d'Orange repeating her Ripon mistake by going too fast too early against stronger pace opposition
Monitor whether Napa gets drawn into the early pace battle rather than sitting handy as his class advantage suggests
Check if Where Love Lives can reproduce his Thirsk form after 48 days off against much stronger pace pressure
Observe whether Oisin Murphy drops Adaay Of Scarlett in behind early rather than making his usual front-running move
Watch for Dandyman Dan and A Bear Affair to be held up longest given the likely strong gallop ahead

races.name: Star Sports Henry II Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Sweet William
runners_data.note: Defending champion with strong recent form but hold-up style faces tactical challenge against lone leader
runners_data.spotlight: Won this in 2024 and has added three more Group-race wins, the latest on reappearance in this month's Sagaro Stakes at Ascot (2m, good to firm) where he was clear with subsequent Group 1 winner Caballo De Mar; leading claims despite 5lb penalty.

runners_data.name: Furthur
runners_data.note: Hold-up style struggling for form since August Group 3 win, needs strong pace to be effective
runners_data.spotlight: He hasn't kicked on since beating Epic Poet to win the Group 3 Geoffrey Freer at Newbury (1m5f, good to firm) last August and failed to threaten when fourth in the Yorkshire Cup at York three weeks ago; however, he could improve for that first outing since finishing mid-division in the Melbourne Cup (gelded between those starts); this 4yo remains one to be interested in.

runners_data.name: Epic Poet
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer but ten straight Group race defeats suggest he's become a bridesmaid
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten in Group races on his last ten starts but went close in the Yorkshire Cup at York (1m6f, good to firm) last May and he was a good third in that same Group 2 a fortnight ago (good); he should be fine back up in trip and might not be far away.

runners_data.name: Lazy Griff
runners_data.note: Only front runner returning from 333-day break, but Derby form gives him class edge if fit
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up in the Derby at Epsom (1m4f, good) last June and kept on well for third in the Irish Derby at the Curragh (1m4f, good) later that month; absent since but this lightly raced 4yo could be suited by the step up in trip and he's a major player if ready to rumble after his absence.

runners_data.name: Paradias
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but good Sandown record, AW form suggests retention of ability despite age
runners_data.spotlight: 7yo who has a good record here and has been better than ever in AW handicaps this year, and he wasn't beaten far when fifth of six in Group 2 Jockey Club Stakes at Newmarket (1m4f, good to firm) four weeks ago; however, his form needs to go to a new level and he's unraced beyond 1m4f on the Flat.

runners_data.name: Dubai Future
runners_data.note: 10-year-old hold-up horse well past prime, early Meydan form now distant memory
runners_data.spotlight: Won Group 3 (1m6f, good) and Group 2 (2m, good) races at Meydan early last year and he's very much of interest on that form; however, not at the same level subsequently and he was a soundly beaten fourth behind Sweet William in the Group 3 Sagaro at Ascot (2m, good to firm) recently.

runners_data.name: Beylerbeyi
runners_data.note: Non-runner
runners_data.spotlight: Won the Cesarewitch Handicap (2m2f, good to firm) last October and some very solid AW form this year; he's better than he showed in the Group 3 Ormonde Stakes at Chester (1m5f, good) three weeks ago, when tailed off at 50-1, but on ratings he's down the pecking order in this line-up.

runners_data.name: Duke Of Oxford
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with recent AW progress but turf form remains questionable
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive on AW in the winter with 2m handicap wins at Kempton and Newcastle; however, only fifth of 12 at Newcastle (2m) last month and the suitability of turf is questionable.

races.paceDynamic: Lazy Griff is the only confirmed front runner in this 8-runner field and will have an uncontested lead from the start. With all other runners preferring hold-up tactics, Lazy Griff can dictate a steady, sustainable gallop through the early stages without pressure. The pace will build gradually as the hold-up horses begin their moves from 3f out, creating a tactical race where positioning and timing matter more than raw speed. This race shape strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can avoid the traffic problems that will inevitably develop in the large pack of hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lazy Griff Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Lazy Griff gets an easy early lead and dictates moderate fractions
scenarios.body: He can kick clear turning for home before the hold-up brigade get organised, and his class will tell in the final furlong. The absence since June becomes irrelevant if he gets first run on his rivals.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-up Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large pack of hold-up horses creates a messy, stop-start finish with limited room
scenarios.body: The best horse in the scrum will emerge late, likely Sweet William who has Havlin's big-race experience to find the gaps. Dubai Future could also benefit from Probert's tactical nous.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Early Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Lazy Griff goes too slow early and gets swamped by the field at the 2f pole
scenarios.body: This becomes a sprint finish where the horse with most natural speed will prevail over this shorter-than-ideal distance. Furthur's recent run suggests he has the pace for this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Upset from Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If one of the outsiders gets a perfect stalking trip just behind Lazy Griff
scenarios.body: Paradias or Duke Of Oxford could exploit their better position relative to the main hold-up pack. Their AW form suggests they retain ability despite lower ratings.

watchPoints.text: Lazy Griff's fitness after 333 days off - any signs of blowing up in final furlong could open door
Traffic problems developing from 2f pole with seven hold-up horses converging simultaneously
Sweet William's position turning for home - needs Havlin to find clear path to utilise finishing kick
Early pace - if Lazy Griff goes too conservatively he invites pressure from the field
Dubai Future showing any signs of his old Meydan form in the closing stages

races.name: Star Sports Heron Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Wise Prince
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning to form after 14 days off, needs strong pace to set up his finishing kick
runners_data.spotlight: Promising win at Nottingham (1m, good to soft) last October on sole 2yo start and showed up very well before fading into third in the Group 3 Classic Trial here (1m2f, good) on his reappearance; pulled hard and weakened when finishing last in the Group 2 Dante at York (1m2f, good) a fortnight ago; this drop back in trip looks the right move and he retains potential.

runners_data.name: Time To Turn
runners_data.note: Proven Group 3 winner but 215 days off creates fitness concerns despite Appleby's record with returning horses
runners_data.spotlight: Made it three wins from his six 2yo starts when landing the Group 3 Horris Hill at Newbury (7f, soft) last October; has also won on good ground; carries a 5lb penalty on his reappearance and Talk Of New York may be his top yard's chief hope, but he won with something to spare at Newbury and could have a part to play.

runners_data.name: Talk Of New York
runners_data.note: Front-runner with tactical pace who can lead or sit handy, headgear change adds extra focus
runners_data.spotlight: Impressive at Kempton (1m, AW) last October on sole 2yo start and returned with close Listed third at Meydan (1m, good) before comfortable conditions race win at Newmarket (7f, good) where he settled better in a first-time hood (retained); that latest form hasn't worked out well but he is William Buick's mount of the four Godolphin runners and is a key player.

runners_data.name: Andab
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in excellent current form with 3lb penalty, Murphy booking suggests strong chance
runners_data.spotlight: Listed winner at Dundalk (7f, AW) last October and running well in defeat this year, particularly at the Curragh (1m, good; Listed) this month when 2l runner-up in first-time cheekpieces (retained); with a clear run he'd have finished closer last time and holds each-way claims under a 3lb penalty.

runners_data.name: Nation's Hope
runners_data.note: Unbeaten front-runner taking significant class rise, most vulnerable if pace gets competitive
runners_data.spotlight: 5l win on debut at Kempton (1m, AW) last November and made all by 6l in novice there (1m) the following month; takes a steep rise in grade this evening and most of today's rivals have greater substance to their form, including two of his stablemates, but it remains to be seen where his limitations lie and he's an interesting contender.

runners_data.name: Yazin
runners_data.note: In-form front-runner with recent conditions race win, Moore's presence confirms stable confidence
runners_data.spotlight: Two novice wins last autumn (7f, good to soft/good) and he comfortably completed the hat-trick when making all in a warm, three-runner conditions race at Southwell (1m, AW) on last month's reappearance; in top hands (one of two for the yard) and he could take this rise in grade in his stride.

runners_data.name: Golden Knight
runners_data.note: Unexposed leader returning after 218 days break, biggest unknown in the field
runners_data.spotlight: Promising fourth on debut at Haydock (1m, good to soft) last September and built on that to make all by nearly 2l at Newmarket (1m, good) in October; unexposed and could have more to offer but has plenty to find today.

runners_data.name: Padraig Dawn
runners_data.spotlight: Won on debut at Southwell (7f, AW) in February and went close in Listed race (1m, AW) at Newcastle; soundly beaten eighth of 14 at 40-1 in the 2,000 Guineas at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) this month but he was far from disgraced and is not ruled out back down in grade.

runners_data.name: Maximized
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose recent form shows him finishing held, needs career-best effort here
runners_data.spotlight: Won last May/June on first two starts and some creditable runs since, but he's finished held at Newmarket on both outings this spring (7f, good/good to firm), including behind stablemate Talk Of New York; others preferred.

races.paceDynamic: Yazin, Talk Of New York, Nation's Hope and Golden Knight will ensure a strong gallop from the start, with Yazin and Nation's Hope particularly keen to lead having both made all in recent wins. The sustained pace over this mile trip will test stamina reserves, especially with Talk Of New York adding pressure from a prominent position. Time To Turn and Wise Prince possess the strongest closing kicks but will need the pace to collapse late. This race shape clearly favours horses with tactical speed and the ability to travel kindly in the slipstream before finishing, penalising pure front-runners and rewarding prominent racers who can quicken.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the four pace-setters go too hard early and weaken markedly in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop sets up perfectly for the hold-up horses with proven finishing kicks. Time To Turn's Group 3-winning form and Wise Prince's Gosden training give them the class edge when the pace falters.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If Yazin or Talk Of New York show restraint early and the pace becomes more measured.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a tactical affair where horses with both pace and stamina can position ideally. Talk Of New York's versatility and Andab's Listed-winning form make them perfectly suited to this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sustained Gallop Favours
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays strong but even throughout, testing stamina without complete collapse.
scenarios.body: Horses who can travel well in behind but have the engine to sustain their effort benefit most. Andab's recent Listed form and Maximized's prominent style suit this grinding finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the leaders gets first run and the others fail to respond quickly enough.
scenarios.body: A horse breaks clear in the straight and holds on despite the strong pace. Yazin's recent front-running success and superior recent form make him the most likely to achieve this.

watchPoints.text: Nation's Hope may set unsustainable fractions if allowed an uncontested lead given his inexperience at this level
Time To Turn's 215-day break is significant despite Appleby's excellent record with returning horses
Yazin and Talk Of New York could engage in early pace battle that compromises both of their chances
Golden Knight's 218-day absence makes him the biggest form unknown despite his previous promise
Wise Prince showed signs of inexperience fading late in the Classic Trial and needs to prove his stamina

races.name: Star Sports Brigadier Gerard Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Ombudsman
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with Group 1 class advantage but 61 days off and needs the race to unfold perfectly
runners_data.spotlight: Second in this last year on his reappearance and he's won three Group 1 races since (1m2f/1m1f, good to firm/good), the latest the Dubai Turf at Meydan in March on his sole outing this year; John Gosden has said that this is "going to bring him on to where we want him at (Royal) Ascot" but he'll be very tough to beat under a 7lb penalty if close to the top of his game.

runners_data.name: Gethin
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who looked sharp on reappearance at Kempton and suits this intermediate distance perfectly
runners_data.spotlight: 2-2 (heavy/good) prior to finishing second in two Listed races last autumn (1m4f/1m2f, very soft/good to soft); reappeared with convincing Listed win at Kempton (1m2f, AW), an improved performance which bodes very well for his future prospects; acquired by Wathnan Racing since that last run; respected.

runners_data.name: Bedouin Prince
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner who will dictate terms but faces stronger opposition than recent Dubai/Bahrain efforts
runners_data.spotlight: Very lightly raced 4yo who went close in a handicap at Meydan in January (1m2f, good; behind Arabian Light) and did likewise in a Listed race in Bahrain (1m3f, good to firm) in February; however, further improvement is required if he's to make a serious impact this evening.

runners_data.name: Wimbledon Hawkeye
runners_data.note: Prominent type returning from 208-day break with headgear applied, consistency suggests readiness but rust concerns
runners_data.spotlight: Admirably consistent in defeat in Group races last year before winning the Grade 3 Nashville Derby at Kentucky (10.5f, firm) last August; well beaten in the Breeders' Cup Turf next time; has an each-way shout if fully tuned up for this reappearance outing.

runners_data.name: Arabian Light
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with recent Meydan form that directly relates to Bedouin Prince's form line
runners_data.spotlight: Beat Bedouin Prince to win handicap at Meydan (1m2f, good) in January and very close second in Group 3 there (1m2f, good) later that month; this 5yo has had just ten starts and further improvement cannot be ruled out, but a career best is necessary if he's to come out on top today.

runners_data.name: Almeric
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose form has stalled on good going, raising questions about surface preference
runners_data.spotlight: Three wins (1m-1m2f, soft/good to soft) from his first four starts, including two Listed races; his progress has stalled on good going on his two starts since but one was the Group 1 Champion Stakes and the other was last month's reappearance (here); it's too soon to label him a slow-ground specialist and he's not written off in view of his abundant earlier promise.

races.paceDynamic: Bedouin Prince will set a steady, sustainable pace from the front with no other confirmed pace-setters to pressure him early. The prominently-raced Gethin, Wimbledon Hawkeye and Almeric will track behind in a compact group, while hold-up horses Ombudsman and Arabian Light settle at the back. This creates a rhythm that builds gradually, with the real pace injection coming from the 2f pole as the field compresses. The shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce sustained finishing kicks, as they'll have plenty of horse left when the race ignites.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Bedouin Prince maintains an even gallop and the pace stays modest until the 2f marker
scenarios.body: The closers get perfect positioning as the field comes back to them late, with Ombudsman and Arabian Light having maximum tactical advantage. Their superior class tells when they can unleash full finishing efforts.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Victory
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens from the 4f pole as the prominent runners apply early pressure on Bedouin Prince
scenarios.body: This sustained tempo stretches the field and blunts the kick of the hold-up horses who face too much ground to make up. Gethin or Almeric can dictate from their ideal tracking positions and kick clear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays
scenarios.trigger: If Bedouin Prince gets soft fractions and the field hesitates to challenge until too late
scenarios.body: The leader gets a dream run and finds enough in the tank when the challengers finally come, benefiting from racing on his own terms. His class from narrow defeats in better company shows through.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If nobody wants to race and they crawl through the early stages before a mad dash home
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint finish over 2f where tactical position matters more than stamina, creating chaos. Any horse with early speed positioning gains a crucial edge.

watchPoints.text: Bedouin Prince getting easy fractions through the first 6f could set up his front-running tactics perfectly
Ombudsman's jumping from the gates after 61 days off - any slow start kills his hold-up strategy
Wimbledon Hawkeye showing ring rustiness in the preliminaries after 208 days away from action
Ryan Moore's positioning on Arabian Light in the early stages will signal confidence levels
The pace through the first 4f - anything significantly slower than even gallop favours the closers

races.name: Starsports.Bet Whitsun Cup Handicap

runners_data.name: Hickory
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who thrived in this race last year but needs to bounce back from disappointing Ascot return 19 days ago
runners_data.spotlight: Third in this last year and improved form later in the season, finishing his campaign in fine form (on various ground); down the field at Ascot on recent return but he was hampered and may have needed the run; not discounted.

runners_data.name: Raammee
runners_data.note: Sole pace-setter returning from 262-day layoff but those all-weather wins showed genuine class and he faces much easier task
runners_data.spotlight: Won on debut at Kempton (1m, AW) last August and easily justified 1-9 odds in a novice at Newcastle (1m, AW) in September; his opening mark is a lofty one but he has the potential to be better than it; respected on return.

runners_data.name: Nostrum
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse struggling to recapture Group 3 form but showed glimpses of old ability in Victoria Cup seasonal debut
runners_data.spotlight: Group 3 runner-up in June 2024; nothing like the same force subsequently but some encouragement can be taken from his stable/seasonal debut in the Victoria Cup at Ascot, where he was soundly beaten overall but was first of seven in the group that raced initially on the far side; he's not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Saytarr
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who excels on artificial surfaces but remains winless on turf from nine attempts despite recent Ascot third
runners_data.spotlight: He won earlier this year on his first three starts for James Horton (7f/1m, AW); made it 0-9 on turf when 2l third of 11 at Ascot (1m, good to firm) four weeks ago but that was still a positive run and he could be in the mix.

runners_data.name: Cogitate
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer under top jockey William Buick who needs to improve on recent turf form but has winning form at this level
runners_data.spotlight: He needs to produce more than he's managed back on turf on his last two starts but prior to those he was a good second at Kempton (7f, AW) in March, and he won on grass at Salisbury (1m, good to firm) last May; capable of having a say if getting back to his best.

runners_data.name: Boyfriend
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with proven form at this mark but returning from 40-day break following disappointing Spring Cup effort
runners_data.spotlight: Consistent across his five starts last year and won off this mark at Nottingham (1m, good) last June; reappeared with close eighth of 24 in the Spring Cup at Newbury (1m, good) and could build on that effort today; chance.

runners_data.name: Dark Tornado
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with excellent going record who should improve significantly for recent seasonal reappearance at Newmarket
runners_data.spotlight: There was no return to his peak form on his recent stable and seasonal debut at Newmarket (7f, good) but it wasn't a bad performance and he could improve for that run; might not be far away; watch the betting.

races.paceDynamic: Raammee will lead from the start with no other confirmed pace-setters in this small field, allowing him to dictate a comfortable gallop through the early stages. The five hold-up horses (Hickory, Nostrum, Saytarr, Cogitate, Boyfriend, Dark Tornado) will settle behind in a compact group, creating a patient waiting game. This sustainable pace will set up a sprint finish from the 2f pole as the hold-up brigade unleash their kicks simultaneously. This race shape strongly favours horses with proven finishing kicks who can produce their best work in the final 2f when the pace lifts.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Comfortable Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Raammee maintains his advantage turning for home and the chasers can't close the gap quickly enough
scenarios.body: The patient early pace plays perfectly into the leader's hands as his 262-day break becomes irrelevant over this shorter trip. His class from those dominant all-weather wins proves decisive as the hold-up horses struggle to peg him back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Kick Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses time their challenges perfectly and overwhelm Raammee in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The sustainable early pace sets up a genuine sprint finish where class and tactical speed become paramount. Fresh legs and superior finishing kicks prove decisive as Raammee pays for his early exertions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Raammee Folds Early
scenarios.trigger: If Raammee's long absence tells and he weakens noticeably from 3f out
scenarios.body: The leader's stamina gives way unexpectedly, turning this into a muddling affair where the first to move wins decisively. Dark Tornado's recent run and good going record makes him perfectly placed to capitalize.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If one of the hold-up horses breaks ranks early and steals a march on the field
scenarios.body: An unexpected early move catches the field flat-footed and creates an unassailable advantage. The tactical element trumps pure class as connections show their hand before rivals can respond.

watchPoints.text: Raammee's jumping and early position - if he misses the break or gets bustled early, his whole race plan collapses
How quickly the hold-up horses can close on Raammee in the final 2f - their ability to produce instant acceleration will determine the outcome
Hickory's early positioning - if Saffie Osborne gets him closer than usual it suggests confidence in his fitness
Dark Tornado's improvement from his recent run - any sharper move suggests the stable fancied this as a winning opportunity
The pace through the middle section - if Raammee quickens unexpectedly at halfway it will test the stamina of his pursuers

races.name: Starsports.Bet Handicap

runners_data.name: Luzon Heights
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with proven class from Ascot second, suits the expected traffic chaos perfectly
runners_data.spotlight: Picked up a Southwell nursery (AW) in September and after a solid comeback at Newmarket in April he posted his best effort yet when second at Ascot (also 1m, good) three weeks ago; improving colt who is much respected.

runners_data.name: Suddenly I See
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with William Buick, but faces severe congestion issues with similar-styled rivals
runners_data.spotlight: Signed off last term by landing a Musselburgh maiden (7f) and reappeared at that track when making a winning handicap debut (1m, also good) in April; raised to this mark when only sixth at Beverley next time but softer conditions were a plausible excuse; not dismissed back on a sounder surface with William Buick taking over.

runners_data.name: The Joker
runners_data.note: Proven at course but prominent style puts him right in the danger zone for traffic problems
runners_data.spotlight: 0-6 record includes three runs here but he's run well on all of those visits, including when third of six in a hot Class 4 on his April return; filled that position again at Newmarket (also 1m2f, good) 12 days ago and this free-going sort may benefit from today's drop back to 1m; player.

runners_data.name: Darzah
runners_data.note: Inexperienced prominent runner from powerful Haggas stable, congestion likely to hinder development
runners_data.spotlight: Her debut fifth at Newmarket (good) was a promising effort in April and she had little difficulty getting off the mark when scoring at Bath (also 1m, firm) a fortnight ago; still a touch raw that day and she brings plenty of potential to this handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Law Court
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent performer but already faced traffic issues at Newbury last time
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to score but he's been in the frame all four starts and ran well when second at Newbury (1m, good) on his handicap debut 12 days ago; made his bid on a part of the track that was possibly unfavoured that day and looks sure to make his presence felt again.

runners_data.name: Brighlee
runners_data.note: Prominent style conflicts with race shape, 40-day break adds tactical uncertainty under pressure
runners_data.spotlight: Chased home a subsequent Listed winner at Salisbury (1m, good to firm) in August but disappointed in October after a break; plugged on without threatening when fifth at Nottingham on her reappearance in April and she'll need to tap back into that Salisbury promise to make an impact on this handicap debut; newly fitted hood might help, though.

runners_data.name: Brave Hunter
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up horse with Oisin Murphy, perfectly positioned to exploit traffic chaos ahead
runners_data.spotlight: Made a big move at halfway but stuck to his task when second of 12 at Windsor (1m, good to firm; winner was completing a four-timer) 17 days ago; that was his handicap debut and first go at 1m so plenty of optimism he can progress again with Oisin Murphy taking over.

runners_data.name: Blues And Royals
runners_data.note: Flexible style allows tactical options, recent AW win shows current form progression
runners_data.spotlight: Dual AW winner this year but he's fine on turf too and ran creditably when second of ten at Musselburgh (again 1m, good) in April; up 5lb for latest Kempton success three weeks ago but likely he can do better again.

runners_data.name: Trio
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner but faces early battle with Loblolly which could compromise finish
runners_data.spotlight: Leicester maiden (good to soft) winner in October but she's been stuck in third place since, including when she came up against Blues And Royals at Kempton (again 1m, AW) three weeks ago; should give her running while finding one or two stronger again.

runners_data.name: Montague Menace
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse but poor recent handicap form suggests limited competitiveness despite style advantage
runners_data.spotlight: Took a 7f Lingfield maiden (AW) on his comeback in March but bombed out when strong in the market on his handicap debut at Epsom (8.5f, good) next time; finished 12th of 14 at York a fortnight ago and has a point to prove now.

runners_data.name: Loblolly
runners_data.note: Front runner returning from 53-day break, fitness concerns against sharper rivals after layoff
runners_data.spotlight: Gained due reward for a couple of close calls when making all for a convincing win at Lingfield (7f, AW) in September; beaten around 17l on his next two starts, however, including in a warm event at Southwell on his April return (had been gelded); needs to get back on track.

runners_data.name: Crimson Rambler
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with light weight but 37-day gap and trainer's modest strike rate raise questions
runners_data.spotlight: Won twice on AW within five days in March and carried on his progression back on turf when second of 12 at Nottingham (also about 1m, good) in April; might have found 1m2f a slight stretch when third on his final start for George Scott and subsequently secured for 20,000gns; he's back at 1m but up in grade for this stable debut.

races.paceDynamic: Trio and Loblolly will dispute the early lead with five prominent racers (Suddenly I See, The Joker, Darzah, Law Court, Brighlee) creating significant congestion behind them. The pace will be honest rather than searching, but the bunching of prominent runners means traffic problems are inevitable approaching the home turn. This tactical bottleneck will favor the hold-up horses who can stay out of trouble and deliver late challenges when the prominent brigade gets squeezed. The race shape clearly benefits closers who can find clear running.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent brigade gets tangled up turning for home as expected.
scenarios.body: The pace setters fade after honest gallop while traffic chaos allows patient tactics to prosper. Clean passages for the back markers become decisive as front runners compromise each other.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Escape Early
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent runners gets first run before the squeeze develops.
scenarios.body: Suddenly I See or The Joker uses class to kick clear before congestion hits behind them. The winner avoids trouble by making their move at the perfect moment when others hesitate.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scenario
scenarios.trigger: If Trio and Loblolly go too hard early and stop dramatically.
scenarios.body: The genuine pace setters empty out leaving a moderate gallop that suits horses who can quicken. Mid-division runners benefit from the softened pace and get competitive late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Trio or Loblolly gets soft fractions and the field fails to pressure them.
scenarios.body: The leader conserves energy in the early stages then kicks when the prominent runners start struggling. Superior tactical ride allows front runner to exploit divided chasing pack.

watchPoints.text: Trio and Loblolly setting unsustainable fractions if they engage in early speed duel
Prominent quintet creating traffic jam 2-3 furlongs out when they all need racing room simultaneously
Suddenly I See and The Joker getting squeezed despite having the class to win if finding clear passage
Luzon Heights and Brave Hunter traveling smoothly in rear, positioned perfectly if pace scenario unfolds as expected
Darzah handling the step up in class and tactical pressure on just her second career start
